Our revenue comes from several places: Fixed-bid excavation and utility jobs Emergency water line calls billed same day Time-and-materials work Equipment rentals Material sales and delivery Remodel and addition contracts Each one has its own billing rhythm, cost structure, and tax treatment. You will bring order, accuracy, and insight to all of it. This is a fully remote position. Your work will shape how we price jobs, manage cash, invest in equipment, and grow. Prepare monthly work-in-progress (WIP) schedules, including over and under billings, using percentage-of-completion revenue recognition under ASC 606. Analyze estimated versus actual costs by job and service line, and flag margin erosion early. Build internal equipment cost rates (ownership, fuel, maintenance, and operator time) so machine costs are charged accurately to jobs. Partner with Doug and Mike on bid pricing feedback, using historical job cost data to sharpen future estimates. Billing, Receivables, and Payables Oversee customer invoicing across fixed-bid, time-and-materials, emergency service, rental, and material delivery work. Oversee AP, including vendor and subcontractor payments, lien waivers, and subcontractor insurance and W-9 compliance. Equipment and Fixed Assets Maintain the fixed asset register for our excavators, skid steers, trucks, trailers, and rental fleet. Track depreciation (book and tax), equipment financing, and rental fleet utilization and profitability. Support repair-versus-replace and buy-versus-rent decisions with clear cost analysis. Tax, Payroll, and Compliance Prepare and file Washington State excise tax returns, including B&O tax and sales and use tax. Manage Washington L&I workers’ compensation reporting and coordinate insurance audits. Keep contractor registration, bonding, and insurance documentation current, and support bonding capacity reviews. Prepare 1099s and coordinate with our outside CPA on annual tax filings and any reviews or audits. Cash, Budgeting, and Strategy Manage weekly cash flow forecasting, with attention to seasonal swings in Pacific Northwest construction. Build the annual budget and track performance against it. Develop KPIs and dashboards for ownership: job margin, equipment utilization, AR days, backlog, and emergency call profitability. Identify process improvements and help modernize our accounting systems and workflows as we grow. What You Bring Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience. 5+ years of progressive accounting experience, including at least 2 years in construction, contracting, or project-based accounting. Hands-on experience with job costing, WIP schedules, and percentage-of-completion revenue recognition. Strong command of GAAP and full-cycle accounting. Experience with construction accounting software such as QuickBooks (Online or Contractor Edition), Sage 100/300 Contractor, Foundation, or Sage Intacct Construction. Advanced Excel skills, including pivot tables, lookups, and building clean, reusable schedules. Ability to work independently in a remote setting, manage deadlines, and communicate financial results in plain language to owners who think in yards of dirt, not debits and credits. Sound judgment, discretion with confidential information, and a high standard of accuracy. Nice to Have CPA, CMA, or progress toward certification. Experience with Washington State B&O and sales tax rules for contractors. Background with equipment-heavy businesses, rental operations, or heavy civil and utility contractors. Full benefits: Medical, dental, and vision insurance Retirement savings plan with employer contribution Life and disability insurance Generous paid time off and paid holidays Professional development support, including CPA and CMA exam assistance, continuing education, and software training.
